transcript_facts.fact: Patient has had a runny nose and a cough for four days.
Patient's breathing has been going really fast since yesterday.
Patient is seven months old.
Patient had a temperature of 37.9 this morning.
Patient is taking most of his bottles, but only managed about half of each bottle since yesterday.
Patient keeps pulling off to breathe.
Patient has had four wet nappies in the last 24 hours, which is usually six or seven.
Patient's sister had an apnoea with bronchiolitis two years ago.
Patient has no history of severe symptoms like apnoea.
Patient has no gone blue or very pale.
Patient brought up a bit of milk after coughing.
Patient was born at 39 weeks with no problems.
Patient has no cardiac or respiratory history.
Patient's immunisations are up to date.
Patient has taken Calpol once yesterday.
Father smokes, but only outside.
Patient's temperature is 37.8 °C.
Patient's respiratory rate is 54 times a minute.
Patient's heart rate is 150.
Patient's oxygen level is 95 percent.
Patient has mild subcostal recession.
Patient's capillary refill is under two seconds.
Patient is alert.
Patient has bilateral fine crackles and wheeze on both sides of his chest.
Patient is working a bit harder to breathe.
Patient's feeding is down to about half, which is right on the line.
Patient's oxygen is okay and he is alert.
Advice given: Give him smaller feeds more often.
Advice given: Use saline drops in his nose before feeds to help clear it.
Advice given: Bronchiolitis often gets worse over the first three to five days before it gets better.
Safety-netting: Call 999 if he has any pauses in his breathing, goes blue, or is really struggling to breathe.
Safety-netting: Call us or 111 straight away if he's taking less than half his usual feeds, has no wet nappy for 12 hours, or seems more tired and floppy.
